blocks.text: When you configure Private Access (ZPA) to discover applications, the Applications Discovered in Past 14 Days widget in the Applications dashboard displays the applications that Private Access discovered for your organization. Discovered applications are listed from most to least recent.
You can click a discovered application to view its diagnostics.
If an application was discovered over 14 days in the past, then the User Activity diagnostics corresponding to application discovery will not be available.

If you want to define a user access policy for a specific application listed in the Applications Discovered in Past 14 Days widget, or you want to be able to change other settings for it (e.g., enable health reporting or configure bypass settings), you can explicitly define the application within an application segment.
When defining a new application segment, Zscaler recommends taking note of the following interaction between a wildcard domain and specific host domain, where wildcard no longer means wildcard:

blocks.item: You have an application segment defined by a wildcard (*.exapp.company.com).
You add the application segment to an access policy.
You create a new application segment (file.exapp.company.com).

blocks.text: The application segment in the third bullet is not covered by the access policy. By defining the application segment (file.exapp.company.com) separately, you need to add a new access policy because the application is matched to the specific application segment. Private Access always matches an application to the most specific application segment, even if that application could potentially match a wildcard application segment. For policy, Private Access evaluates the policy with the most specific application segment.

Private Access does not apply the ports specified in the application segments that contain IP subnets or wildcards towards application segments that contain more specific IP addresses or FQDNs. You must explicitly specify the ports in the application segment that contain the IP addresses or FQDNs.
To define a discovered application in the Applications dashboard:

blocks.item: In the top navigation bar, click Analytics.
In the left-side navigation, enable Switch to Existing Reports, then go to Private Applications > Applications.
If you do not see the Applications Discovered in Past 14 Days widget on the dashboard, select it from the widgets drop-down menu.
Only 8 widgets can be selected and displayed.
In the Applications Discovered in Past 14 Days widget, click Add Application Segment.
Select the applications you want to define, then click Define Selected Applications.
The Add Application Segment window appears.
In the Add Application Segment window, add an application segment.
